3397-roundabout-to-boston-from-literary-.title: Roundabout To Boston From Literary Friends And Acquaintance
3397-roundabout-to-boston-from-literary-.creator: William Dean Howells
3397-roundabout-to-boston-from-literary-.description: A book by William Dean Howells. Besides those few pitiful successes, I had nothing but defeats in the sort of literature which I supposed was to be my calling, and the defeats threw me upon prose; for some sort of literary thing, if not one, then another, I must do if I lived; and I began to write those studies of Venetian life which afterwards became a book, and which I contributed as letters to the 'Boston Advertiser', after vainly offering them to more aesthetic periodicals.

arxiv-2111-04179.title: The eXtreme Mesh deformation approach (X-MESH) for the Stefan phase change model
arxiv-2111-04179.creator: Nicolas Moës, Jean-François Remacle, Jonathan Lambrechts, Benoît Lé, Nicolas Chevaugeon
arxiv-2111-04179.description: Abstract The eXtreme Mesh deformation approach (X-MESH) is a new paradigm to follow sharp interfaces without remeshing and without changing the mesh topology. Even though the mesh does not change its topology, it can follow interfaces that do change their topology (nucleation, coalescence, splitting) and that possibly travel over long distances.

arxiv-2203-15100.title: Understanding out-of-distribution accuracies through quantifying difficulty of test samples
arxiv-2203-15100.creator: Berfin Şimşek, Melissa Hall, Levent Sagun
arxiv-2203-15100.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Berfin Şimşek, Melissa Hall, Levent Sagun. Existing works show that although modern neural networks achieve remarkable generalization performance on the in-distribution (ID) dataset, the accuracy drops significantly on the out-of-distribution (OOD) datasets [ 1 , 2 ] . To understand why a variety of models consistently make more mistakes in the OOD datasets, we propose a new metric to quantify the difficulty of the test images (either ID or OOD) that depends on the interaction of the training dataset and the model.

arxiv-2306-03950.title: Misgendered : Limits of Large Language Models in Understanding Pronouns
arxiv-2306-03950.creator: Tamanna HossainUniversity of California, Irvine tthossai@uci.edu, Sunipa DevGoogle Research sunipadev@google.com, Sameer SinghUniversity of California, Irvine sameer@uci.edu
arxiv-2306-03950.description: Abstract Content Warning: This paper contains examples of misgendering and erasure that could be offensive and potentially triggering. Gender bias in language technologies has been widely studied, but research has mostly been restricted to a binary paradigm of gender. It is essential also to consider non-binary gender identities, as excluding them can cause further harm to an already marginalized group.

arxiv-2311-14389.title: Precision Top Mass Measurement Using Energy Correlators
arxiv-2311-14389.creator: Dennis Schwarz
arxiv-2311-14389.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Dennis Schwarz. Precision top mass measurements at hadron colliders have been notoriously difficult. The fundamental challenge in the current approaches lies in achieving simultaneously high top mass sensitivity and good theoretical control. Inspired by the use of standard candles in cosmology, we overcome this problem by showing that a single energy correlator-based observable can be constructed that reflects the characteristic angular scales associated with both the W W -boson and top quark.

arxiv-2401-05996.description: Abstract We show that phase separation in ordered polar active fluids belongs to a new universality class. arxiv-2505-00532.title: Observation of Resonant Tunneling from Molecular Shape into Vibronic Feshbach Resonances Followed by Mode-Specific Fragmentation
arxiv-2505-00532.creator: Narayan Kundu 1,2, Meenakshi Rana 3, Aryya Ghosh 3, Dhananjay Nandi 1,4
arxiv-2505-00532.description: Abstract We present a kinematically complete study of dissociative electron attachment (DEA) in linear OCS molecules, focusing on how electrons resonantly attach and trigger dissociation. Near the Franck-Condon regime, DEA is dominated by molecular shape resonances, where transient OCS - states form with high vibrational amplitudes, spectroscopically evident as broad features in DEA cross-sections.

arxiv-2507-12595.title: Enhancing In-Domain and Out-Domain EmoFake Detection via Cooperative Multilingual Speech Foundation Models
arxiv-2507-12595.creator: Orchid Chetia, Mohd Mujtaba, Girish*, Arun Balaji
arxiv-2507-12595.description: Abstract In this work, we address EmoFake Detection (EFD). We hypothesize that multilingual speech foundation models (SFMs) will be particularly effective for EFD due to their pre-training across diverse languages, enabling a nuanced understanding of variations in pitch, tone, and intensity. To validate this, we conduct a comprehensive comparative analysis of state-of-the-art (SOTA) SFMs.

arxiv-2512-00486.creator: Yan-Xiao Wang, Yin Zhong
arxiv-2512-00486.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yan-Xiao Wang, Yin Zhong. Heavy-fermion superconductors often display upper critical fields that exceed the conventional Pauli paramagnetic limit, indicating that strong correlations and hybridized quasiparticle bands play an essential role in the paramagnetic pair-breaking process.

pmc-10573267.title: Mesenchymal Stem Cells in the Treatment of COVID-19
pmc-10573267.creator: Bei-Cyuan Guo, Kang-Hsi Wu, Chun-Yu Chen, Wen-Ya Lin, Yu-Jun Chang, Tai-An Lee, Mao-Jen Lin, Han-Ping Wu
pmc-10573267.description: Since the emergence of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, many lives have been tragically lost to severe infections. The COVID-19 impact extends beyond the respiratory system, affecting various organs and functions. In severe cases, it can progress to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and multi-organ failure, often fueled by an excessive immune response known as a cytokine storm.

pmc-10575153.title: Challenges and Opportunities behind the Use of Herbaria in Paleogenomics Studies
pmc-10575153.creator: Simone Papalini, Valerio Di Vittori, Alice Pieri, Marina Allegrezza, Giulia Frascarelli, Laura Nanni, Elena Bitocchi, Elisa Bellucci, Tania Gioia, Luis Guasch Pereira, Karolina Susek, Maud Tenaillon, Kerstin Neumann, Roberto Papa, Andreas W Ebert
pmc-10575153.description: Paleogenomics focuses on the recovery, manipulation, and analysis of ancient DNA (aDNA) from historical or long-dead organisms to reconstruct and analyze their genomes. The aDNA is commonly obtained from remains found in paleontological and archaeological sites, conserved in museums, and in other archival collections.

pmc-11517769.title: Influence of vegetable knowledge in preschooler’s vegetable consumption: Veggies4myHeart project
pmc-11517769.creator: R Novo, J Edra, L Vieito, M Lages, M P Guarino, S Simões Dias, C Braga-Pontes
pmc-11517769.description: BackgroundVegetable consumption among children is below recommended. Food rejection, especially vegetables, is common in preschool-aged children. Impoverished food knowledge is associated with this rejection. The Veggies4myHeart project aims to promote vegetable consumption and knowledge among preschoolers’. This study assesses the project’s effectiveness in increasing vegetable knowledge and consumption and whether increased knowledge influences vegetable consumption.

pmc-12469481.title: Comorbidities and Pregnancy-Related Risk Factors in Patients with Severe Maternal Morbidity: Application of a Validated Obstetrical Comorbidity Scoring System to a Surveillance-Identified Population
pmc-12469481.creator: Carrie Wolfson, Jessica Tsipe Angelson, Alexandra D Forrest, Erin D Michos, Saifuddin Ahmed, Abimbola Aina-Mumuney, Andreea A Creanga
pmc-12469481.description: Background/Objectives: Patient characteristics—especially comorbidities—influence the risk of severe maternal morbidity (SMM). Recent efforts have sought to derive an obstetric comorbidity score to be used for case-mix adjustment. We assess the use of a validated obstetric comorbidity index among patients with SMM and identify additional conditions that could be included in the index.

pmc-12590770.title: Long-term efficacy of anterior nucleus of the thalamus deep brain stimulation in drug-resistant epilepsy: a 5-year multicenter study
pmc-12590770.creator: Tianqi Hu, Hutao Xie, Ming Shan, Lin Sang, Bowen Yang, Quan Zhang, Dongmei Gao, Yuanyuan Jiao, Qinglong Guo, Sizhe Li, Yuxin Wang, Xinnan Du, Anchao Yang, Fangang Meng, Jianguo Zhang, Kai Zhang, Hua Zhang
pmc-12590770.description: BackgroundDeep brain stimulation (DBS) of the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT-DBS) has demonstrated potential in reducing seizure frequency (SF) in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). This multicenter retrospective study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the long-term effects of ANT-DBS on seizure reduction and neuropsychological outcomes, as well as to identify prognostic factors associated with postoperative efficacy.

pmc-12715050.title: Association between deletions in the preS1/2 region of the hepatitis B virus genome and persistently abnormal ALT levels in patients with chronic hepatitis B treated with nucleos(t)ide analogs
pmc-12715050.creator: Yurina Sato, Kotaro Doi, Jun Inoue, Masashi Ninomiya, Mio Tsuruoka, Kosuke Sato, Masazumi Onuki, Satoko Sawahashi, Keishi Ouchi, Kengo Watanabe, Hirofumi Niitsuma, Atsushi Masamune
pmc-12715050.description: Patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) are at risk of developing hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) during treatment with nucleos(t)ide analogs (NAs). Several factors, including abnormal ALT levels during NA treatment, are associated with HCC risk; however, the mechanisms of ALT abnormalities remain unknown.

pmc-12800044.title: Increased plasma fibronectin mirrors intimal phenotypic switching of vascular smooth muscle cells in moyamoya arteriopathy
pmc-12800044.creator: Caroline Asselman, Jozefien Meersschaut, Patrick Willems, Julien Mortier, Frank Vernaillen, Elisabeth Dhondt, Anne Sieben, Sasha Libbrecht, Esperánza Fernandez, Kris Gevaert, Ward De Spiegelaere, Evelien Van Hamme, Veerle De Herdt, Jo Van Dorpe, Dimitri Hemelsoet, Bart Dermaut, Francis Impens
pmc-12800044.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a rare cerebrovascular disorder characterized by progressive stenosis of large intracranial arteries and formation of fragile collateral vessels that can be triggered by a broad range of genetic and immune factors. Central to MMD pathology is excessive proliferation of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) in the intima of affected arteries associated with contractile-to-synthetic phenotypic switching, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear.

pmc-13233441.title: Serum BDNF as an integrative neuro-immunometabolic marker in adolescent polycystic ovary syndrome: divergent dietary and inflammatory associations across weight phenotypes
pmc-13233441.creator: Małgorzata Mizgier, Dorota Formanowicz, Veronica Sansoni, Grażyna Jarząbek-Bielecka, Giovanni Lombardi, Witold Kędzia, Justyna Opydo-Szymaczek
pmc-13233441.description: BackgroundPolycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) in adolescence is characterized by hormonal imbalance, low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic dysfunction. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) regulates energy homeostasis and neuroimmune signaling and may act as a neuroimmunometabolic integrator in PCOS.MethodsForty adolescent females with PCOS (26 normal weight and 14 with overweight and obesity) were evaluated.

pmc-13361207.title: Defect-engineered N-CeO2/N-rGO heterostructures for visible-light photocatalytic degradation of 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid: the synergistic roles of ceria vacancies and N-doped graphene interfaces
pmc-13361207.creator: Nguyen Hoang Hao, Nguyen Thi Thu Ha, Nguyen Ngoc Ha, Bui Cong Trinh, Nguyen Thi Nga, Le Minh Cam
pmc-13361207.description: Defect-engineered reduced graphene oxide heterostructures have attracted increasing attention for improving visible-light photocatalytic performance. In this study, nitrogen-doped cerium oxide supported on nitrogen-doped reduced graphene oxide (N-CeO2/N-rGO) was synthesized as an efficient photocatalyst for the degradation of 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) under visible-light irradiation.

pmc-13366682.title: Self-confidence and anxiety in clinical decision-making among nursing students during high-fidelity simulation training: a longitudinal study
pmc-13366682.creator: Geert Van de Weyer, Filip Haegdorens, Senne Vleminckx, Deborah Hilderson, Erik Franck
pmc-13366682.description: BackgroundClinical decision-making is a core nursing competency that develops progressively through education and practice. However, nursing students frequently report reduced self-confidence and increased anxiety when required to make clinical decisions. High-fidelity simulation (HFS) provides a safe, realistic environment to practice clinical decision-making and may influence these psychological determinants.

pmc-13423446.creator: Tomoaki Kaneko, Shuichiro Matoba, Mitsunori Ushigome, Satoru Kagami, Yasuo Nagashima, Kimihiko Yoshida, Yasuyuki Miura, Takayuki Suzuki, Kentaro Watanabe, Kimihiko Funahashi, Yuichiro Otsuka

pmc-13629165.title: Quantitative Characterization of RNA-Splinted Ligation as a Multipurpose Post-Synthetic Strategy for High-Density DNA Microarrays Synthesized by Nucleic Acid Photolithography
pmc-13629165.creator: Arya Das, Mark M. Somoza
pmc-13629165.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Complex arrays of surface-immobilized DNA oligonucleotides are widely used across diverse fields of bioanalytics, particularly for their applications in massively parallel genomic assays ranging from spatial transcriptomics to protein–DNA recognition studies. DNA microarrays produced by photolithography enable the introduction of versatile chemistries and complexities to surfaces with complete spatial control, but are partially constrained by synthetic error rates for longer probe architectures and by incompatibility with photosensitive chemical building blocks commonly used in phosphoramidite chemistry.

pmc-13632046.title: Illness perception of breast cancer among patients receiving treatment in a university teaching hospital, South-west Nigeria: a qualitative phenomenological study
pmc-13632046.creator: Deborah Tolulope Esan, Oluwatomigbekele Dorcas Onabanjo, Nasirat Omolara Rasaq, Carlos Guillermo Ramos
pmc-13632046.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundBreast cancer remains a significant public health challenge in Nigeria, with perceptions of the illness influencing coping, treatment adherence, and quality of life. Drawing on Leventhal’s Illness Perception Model, this study explored how women diagnosed with breast cancer construct meaning from their experiences, while situating these findings within existing qualitative evidence from Sub-Saharan Africa and addressing a relative gap in phenomenological and theory-informed studies in Nigeria.MethodsA qualitative phenomenological design was employed, involving in-depth interviews with 20 breast cancer patients aged 33–76 years
